## Who this guide is for

You need this guide if you have R code written against synapser 2.x. 3.0 is
not a drop-in upgrade: function names, argument names, and the shape of the
objects you get back have all changed, so an existing script will stop at its
first Synapse call.

The failures are at least loud rather than silent — you'll see
`could not find function "synTableQuery"`,
`unused argument (parentId = "syn123")`, or
`AttributeError: 'File' object has no attribute 'properties'` — and the fixes
are mechanical once you know the four patterns below.

If you're writing new code rather than porting old code, you don't need this
guide at all: start from
[Data Upload, Download, and Delete](data_upload_download.html) and
[Tables](tables.html).

## Why upgrade now

The API changes are what this guide is about, but they aren't the reason to
move. Even setting them aside, staying on 2.x costs you:

- **R dependencies frozen in the past.** 2.x requires `reticulate` between
  1.25 and 1.28 and `rjson` no newer than 0.2.21, pulled from GitHub and the
  CRAN archive through `Remotes:`. An R library holds only one version of a
  package, so installing synapser 2.x pins every other project sharing that
  library to a 2023-era reticulate. 3.0 drops both ceilings and installs from
  CRAN like any other package.
- **A Python ceiling you'll hit sooner or later.** 2.x supports Python
  3.9–3.11 and caps `pandas` at 2.0.3 and `numpy` at 1.24.4, so it cannot be
  installed on a machine whose Python is 3.12 or newer. 3.0 supports Python
  3.10 through 3.14 and declares its Python dependencies through
  `reticulate::py_require()`, so there is no virtualenv to build or repair by
  hand.
- **An old view of Synapse.** 2.x bundles synapseclient 4.4.2; 3.0 tracks
  4.12. Everything the Synapse API has gained in between is unreachable from
  R until you move — and because 3.0 generates its R layer from the Python
  models, that gap stops reopening after this release.

## What you gain in 3.0

Upgrading costs a round of script updates (see below), but it buys you real
capability, not just a version bump:

- **New functionality that 2.x simply didn't have.** Recursive
  `synCopy()`/`synSyncFromSynapse()`/`synWalk()`, hierarchy-wide
  `synDeletePermissions()`/`synListAcl()` with a `dry_run` preview, and JSON
  Schema binding/validation (`synBindSchema()`, `synValidateSchema()`, ...)
  are all new in 3.0 — see
  [New in 3.0: capabilities that didn't exist before](#new-in-30-capabilities-that-didnt-exist-before)
  below. None of these required someone to hand-port them from the Python
  client; they came along for free with the switch to generating the R layer
  directly from `synapseclient.models`.
- **New entity types, not just new methods on the old ones.**
  `VirtualTable`, `DatasetCollection`, `Agent`/`AgentSession`, and
  `SchemaOrganization`/`JSONSchema` have no 2.x counterpart at all, and the
  view types (`EntityView`, `MaterializedView`, `SubmissionView`) replace
  2.x's `EntityViewSchema`/`MaterializedViewSchema`/`SubmissionViewSchema`
  while picking up the same column, query, and ACL verbs as `Table`.
- **Faster access to new Python client features going forward.** Because the
  R layer is generated from the same OOP models the Python client ships,
  new methods and arguments added to `synapseclient` can be surfaced in R
  without waiting on a hand-written wrapper to catch up — which is how the
  gap above accumulated in the first place.
- **One mental model, matching the Python docs.** Every entity — File,
  Folder, Table, Dataset, Project, ... — now follows the same
  `Constructor(...) |> synMethod(...) |> synStore()` shape, with snake_case
  arguments that match the Python client's field names exactly. If the R
  docs for a function are unclear, the
  [Python reference](https://python-docs.synapse.org/) describes the same
  method, argument for argument — that cross-reference didn't reliably work
  in 2.x, where argument names and calling conventions were hand-curated per
  function.

In short, synapser 2.x emphasizes compatibility with an older hand-maintained
API surface, while 3.0 trades one migration pass for long-term gains: fewer
dependency constraints, broader Synapse coverage (new entities plus recursive
and schema workflows), and an API that stays aligned with the actively evolving
Python client instead of drifting behind it.

The rest of this guide covers what to change in existing scripts to get
there.

## Why this release breaks compatibility

Previous versions of synapser wrapped a hand-curated subset of the Python
client behind R-idiomatic function names and camelCase arguments. 3.0
upgrades the reticulate/rjson dependency and, to keep pace with the Python
client's newer `synapseclient.models`/`synapseclient.operations`
architecture, generates the R layer directly from those Python OOP models
instead of maintaining a separate hand-written wrapper. The result is an API
that mirrors the Python client field-for-field, so most existing synapser
scripts will need updates.

This guide covers the Project/Folder/File/Table workflow — the paths most
scripts use. The same patterns apply to every other entity type (Dataset,
Views, Evaluation, Team, Wiki, ...); see the
[full reference](../reference/index.html) for exact signatures.

## Four patterns to relearn

### 1. Instance-first, then pipe

Every entity is now a real object you construct directly — `File(...)`,
`Folder(...)`, `Table(...)`, `Project(...)`, ... — and every operation on it
is a "verb" function (`synStore()`, `synGet()`, `synSetProperties()`,
`synAddColumn()`, `synDeleteRows()`, ...) that takes the instance as its
first argument. You construct the object first, then thread it through
a chain of these verbs with the native pipe, tidyverse-style, instead of
reassigning a variable at every step:

```r
# 2.x -- synStore() was one Python-backed function shared by every entity
# type, with Python duck-typing on `obj` internally; each step reassigned a
# variable rather than chaining
file <- File(path, parentId = "syn123")
file <- synStore(file)
file <- synGet(file$properties$id, downloadFile = FALSE)

# 3.0 -- construct the instance, then pipe it through verbs
file <- File(path = path, parent_id = "syn123") |>
  synStore() |>
  synGet(file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE))
```

This is the change everything else in this guide follows from. Two kinds of
function take an instance this way:

- `synStore()`, `synGet()`, and `synDelete()` are single factory functions
  that accept any supported entity — or, for `synGet()` and `synDelete()`, a
  Synapse ID string instead — and apply the behavior appropriate to that
  entity's type.
- Every other verb (`synAddColumn()`, `synGetAcl()`, `synCopy()`,
  `synWalk()`, `synBindSchema()`, ...) is a generic that dispatches on the
  class of the object you pipe in. The same verb name therefore works
  uniformly across every entity type that supports it, instead of each
  operation being its own hand-written function reconciling the differences
  between entity types internally.

### 2. Properties are no longer nested under `$properties`

```r
# 2.x
entity$properties$id
entity$properties$name

# 3.0
entity$id
entity$name
```

### 3. Arguments are snake_case, matching the Python client exactly

```r
# 2.x
synGet(entity, downloadFile = FALSE)
synStore(obj, forceVersion = FALSE, versionLabel = "2")
File(path, parentId = project$properties$id)

# 3.0
synGet(entity, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE))
synGet(synapse_id) |>
  synSetProperties(version_label = "2", force_version = FALSE) |>
  synStore()
File(path = path, parent_id = project$id)
```

Some arguments moved rather than just changed case. Options that 2.x passed
to `synStore()` — `forceVersion`, `versionLabel` — are fields on the entity
itself in 3.0 (`force_version`, `version_label`), set at construction or with
`synSetProperties()`. `synStore()` itself takes only the entity, an optional
`parent`, and the per-type option objects (`StoreFileOptions()`,
`StoreContainerOptions()`, `StoreTableOptions()`, ...); there is no
`force_version` argument on it.

### 4. Mutation goes through `synSetProperties()`, then an explicit `synStore()`

Directly assigning into `$properties` no longer works. Properties are set
with `synSetProperties()` — which validates the field names against the
object's dataclass fields — and piped into `synStore()`:

```r
# 2.x
entity$properties$name <- "new name"
entity <- synStore(entity)

# 3.0
entity <- synGet(synapse_id) |>
  synSetProperties(name = "new name") |>
  synStore()
```

Table columns are the one exception — those are still mutated in place on
the `$columns` list before `synStore()`:

```r
table$columns[["Expression"]]$name <- "Expression2"
table$columns[["Expression"]]$column_type <- "INTEGER"
table |> synStore()
```

The column verbs `synAddColumn()`, `synDeleteColumn()`, and
`synReorderColumn()` work the same way: they change the table object in place
and return nothing, so they are separate statements rather than links in a
pipe into `synStore()`:

```r
table |> synAddColumn(Column(name = "Expression", column_type = "STRING"))
table |> synStore()
```

## Side-by-side reference: common operations

| Task | 2.x (legacy) | 3.0 (new) |
|---|---|---|
| Create + store an entity | `File(path, parentId = "syn123")` then `synStore(obj)` | `File(path = path, parent_id = "syn123") \|> synStore()` |
| Suppress a new version | `synStore(obj, forceVersion = FALSE)` | `File(path = path, parent_id = "syn123", force_version = FALSE) \|> synStore()` |
| Set name / version label | `entity$properties$name <- "x"; synStore(entity)` | `synGet(id) \|> synSetProperties(name = "x") \|> synStore()` |
| Move an entity | `synMove(entity, newParent)` | `synGet(id) \|> synSetProperties(parent_id = "syn456") \|> synStore()` |
| Track provenance | `synStore(obj, used = "syn123", executed = "syn456")` | `synGet(id) \|> synSetProperties(activity = Activity(used = list("syn123"), executed = list("syn456"))) \|> synStore()` |
| Remove provenance | `synDeleteProvenance(entity)` | `synDisassociateActivityFromEntity(Activity, parent = entity)` |
| Get an entity | `synGet(entity, ...)` | `synGet(synapse_id, file_options = FileOptions(...))` |
| Get a specific version | `synGet(entity, version = 1)` | `synGet(synapse_id, version_number = 1L)` |
| Skip downloading file content | `synGet(entity, downloadFile = FALSE)` | `synGet(synapse_id, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE))` |
| Delete a version only | `synDelete(obj, version = 1)` | `synDelete(entity, version = 1L, version_only = TRUE)` |
| Query a table | `synTableQuery(sql)` | `synQuery(sql)` |
| Create a table column | `synCreateColumn(name = "x", columnType = "STRING")` | `Column(name = "x", column_type = "STRING")` |
| Add a table column | manual list manipulation | `table \|> synAddColumn(Column(name = "x", column_type = "STRING"))`, then `table \|> synStore()` |
| Remove a table column | manual list manipulation | `table \|> synDeleteColumn(name = "x")`, then `table \|> synStore()` |
| Insert-or-update table rows | query, merge, re-store | `table \|> synUpsertRows(values = df, primary_keys = list("Name"))` |
| Build a table from a CSV, inferring columns | `synBuildTable(name, parent, "genes.csv")` | `Table(name = ..., parent_id = ...) \|> synStore() \|> synStoreRows(values = "genes.csv", schema_storage_strategy = "INFER_FROM_DATA")` |

## Removed functions

Because 3.0 generates the R layer from the Python models, a 2.x function
survives only if the models expose an equivalent. These are the removals most
scripts will hit.

### Renamed or restructured

- **`synBuildTable()`** → `Table(...) |> synStore() |> synStoreRows(values = ..., schema_storage_strategy = "INFER_FROM_DATA")`. The table has to exist before rows can be stored into it, so the `synStore()` step is not optional.
- **`synTableQuery()`** → `synQuery()`
- **`synMove()`** → `synSetProperties(parent_id = ...) |> synStore()`
- **`synGetChildren()`** → `synSyncFromSynapse(recursive = FALSE, download_file = FALSE)` and then the container's `$files`/`$folders`, or `synWalk()` to traverse a whole tree
- **`synGetAnnotations()` / `synSetAnnotations()`** → the `annotations` field: read `entity$annotations`, write `synSetProperties(annotations = list(...)) |> synStore()`
- **`synGetProvenance()` / `synSetProvenance()` / `synDeleteProvenance()` / `synUpdateActivity()`** → the `activity` field (an `Activity()` object) set via `synSetProperties()`, and `synDisassociateActivityFromEntity(Activity, parent = entity)` to remove it
- **`synCreateColumn()` / `synCreateColumns()` / `synGetColumn()` / `synGetColumns()` / `synGetTableColumns()`** → the `Column()` constructor and the table's own `$columns` list
- **`synCreateSnapshotVersion()`** → `synSnapshot()`
- **`synRestGET()` / `synRestPOST()` / `synRestPUT()` / `synRestDELETE()`**, and the 2.x `synRestGetAsync()` family → `synRestGet()`, `synRestPost()`, `synRestPut()`, `synRestDelete()`
- **`synCreateTeam()`** → `Team(name = "...") |> synCreate()`; **`synGetTeam()`** → `Team |> synFromId(id)` or `Team |> synFromName(name)`; **`synDeleteTeam()`** → `synDelete(team)`
- **`synSendMembershipInvitation()`** → `synInviteToTeam()`; **`synGetTeamOpenInvitations()`** → `synGetOpenInvitations()`; **`synGetMembershipStatus()`** → `synGetUserMembershipStatus()`
- **`synGetUserProfile()`** → `UserProfile |> synFromId(user_id)` or `UserProfile |> synFromUsername(username)`

Note the calling convention in the last few entries. `synFromId()`,
`synFromName()`, `synFromUsername()`, and
`synDisassociateActivityFromEntity()` wrap Python classmethods, so their
first argument is the *constructor* (`Team`, `UserProfile`, `Activity`) —
that is what selects the implementation — rather than an instance of it.

### Not currently exposed in 3.0

These 2.x functions have no model-layer equivalent yet. Until they get one,
call the [REST API](https://rest-docs.synapse.org/) directly with
`synRestGet()`/`synRestPost()`/`synRestPut()`/`synRestDelete()`, or keep that
step of the pipeline in the Python client:

- **Wikis:** `synGetWiki()`, `synGetWikiHeaders()`, `synGetWikiAttachments()`. The `WikiPage()` constructor and its attachment/markdown helpers exist, but getting or storing a wiki page from R does not.
- **Evaluations and submissions:** `synGetEvaluation()`, `synGetEvaluationByName()`, `synGetEvaluationByContentSource()`, `synSubmit()`, `synGetSubmission()`, `synGetSubmissionStatus()`, `synGetSubmissions()`, `synGetSubmissionBundles()`. `Evaluation(...)` still stores and deletes, and the listing calls — `synGetAllEvaluations()`, `synGetAvailableEvaluations()`, `synGetEvaluationsByProject()`, `synGetUserSubmissions(Submission, evaluation_id)`, `synGetEvaluationSubmissions(Submission, evaluation_id)`, `synGetAllSubmissionStatuses()` — cover most read paths. Fetching a single evaluation or submission by ID, and submitting to a queue, are not available.
- **Storage locations and file handles:** `synCreateS3StorageLocation()`, `synCreateStorageLocationSetting()`, `synSetStorageLocation()`, `synGetMyStorageLocationSetting()`, `synGetProjectSetting()`, `synCreateExternalS3FileHandle()`, `synUploadFileHandle()`, `synGetStsStorageToken()`.
- **Download lists:** `synGetDownloadList()`, `synGetDownloadListManifest()`, `synRemoveFromDownloadList()`, `synClearDownloadList()`.
- **Other:** `synDownloadTableColumns()`, `synGetConfigFile()`, `synInvalidateAPIKey()`.

## New in 3.0: capabilities that didn't exist before

The OOP-model generation doesn't just rename old functions — it also surfaces
Python client functionality that synapser never exposed at all. These
functions have no 2.x equivalent, so there's nothing to migrate *from*, but
existing scripts that worked around their absence (manual recursion to bulk
update ACLs, hand-rolled directory walks, shelling out to `synapseutils` from
Python) can now be simplified.

### Richer access control

`synDeletePermissions()` and `synListAcl()` are new. Both work over a single
entity or an entire container hierarchy at once, so an audit or cleanup that
used to mean writing your own recursive walk over 2.x's `synGetChildren()` — and
getting the edge cases (nested folders, inherited vs. local ACLs) right
yourself — is now one call. `dry_run` lets you preview exactly what a
recursive permissions change will touch before anything is deleted, which
matters once you're operating on an entire project tree instead of a single
entity:

```r
# Preview, then perform, a recursive ACL cleardown of a folder and its children
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synDeletePermissions(recursive = TRUE, include_container_content = TRUE, dry_run = TRUE)
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synDeletePermissions(recursive = TRUE, include_container_content = TRUE)

# List every ACL in a hierarchy, optionally as an ASCII tree
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synListAcl(recursive = TRUE, log_tree = TRUE)
```

One semantic change on an existing function: `synGetPermissions(instance)` now
always returns *your own* effective permissions — the old `principalId`
argument is gone. To check another user or team's permissions, use
`synGetAcl(instance, principal_id = ...)` instead, which still supports it:

```r
# 2.x -- check someone else's permissions
synGetPermissions(entity, principalId = "273948")

# 3.0 -- synGetPermissions() is caller-only; use synGetAcl() for another principal
synGet(synapse_id) |> synGetAcl(principal_id = 273948L)
```

### Container traversal and sync

synapser never exposed `synapseutils`' `copy`, `syncFromSynapse`, or `walk`
utilities — getting this functionality previously meant dropping out of R
into a Python script, or reimplementing the recursion (and its failure
handling) by hand with repeated `synGetChildren()`/`synGet()` calls. In 3.0
they're methods on any container object, so a bulk copy, a full local mirror
of a project, or a metadata-only inventory of an entity tree is a single
pipeline that stays in R:

```r
# Recursively copy a folder, and everything in it, to a new parent
Folder(id = "syn123") |> synCopy(parent_id = "syn456")

# Recursively download a folder tree, populating $files/$folders/$tables/...
folder <- Folder(id = "syn123") |> synSyncFromSynapse(path = "~/local-copy")

# Traverse a hierarchy without downloading anything
for (entry in as.list(folder |> synWalk())) {
  dirpath <- entry[[1]]; dirs <- entry[[2]]; nondirs <- entry[[3]]
  cat(dirpath[[1]], "\n")
}
```

`synWalk()` returns a `GeneratorWrapper` — the same lazy-iterator object 2.x
returned from `synGetChildren()`, which no longer exists. Call `as.list()` on
it to materialize every result into a plain list, or `nextElem()` to pull
results one at a time; you can't loop over it directly the way you can a
list. For the narrower job `synGetChildren()` used to do — listing one
container's immediate children without downloading them — use
`synSyncFromSynapse(recursive = FALSE, download_file = FALSE)` and read the
resulting `$files`/`$folders`.

### JSON Schema binding and validation

Also new: entities can be bound to a JSON Schema and validated against it
directly from R. This lets you enforce metadata/annotation standards on
Files, Folders, and Tables as part of an R pipeline — catching entities with
missing or malformed annotations programmatically instead of relying on
manual review or the web UI — and derive annotation values automatically
from the schema rather than entering them by hand:

```r
folder <- Folder(id = "syn123")
folder |> synBindSchema(json_schema_uri = "myOrg-mySchema-0.0.1")
folder |> synValidateSchema()
folder |> synUnbindSchema()
```

`synBindSchema()` returns the binding record rather than the entity, so bind
the schema as its own statement and keep piping the entity itself.

This applies to Files, Folders, Tables, Projects, and other container/entity
types. Creating the organization and schema themselves uses the new
`SchemaOrganization`/`JSONSchema` constructors — see `?synBindSchema` for a
full example. The rest of the family: `synGetSchema()` and
`synGetSchemaDerivedKeys()` on any bindable entity, plus
`synGetSchemaValidationStatistics()` and `synGetInvalidValidation()` on
containers (Folder, Project).

## Known pitfall: integer literals

R's bare numeric literals (`1`) are doubles. Parameters the Synapse API
expects as integers — `version_number`, `version`, row IDs/versions in
`synDeleteRows(df = ...)` — must use the `L` suffix (`1L`). Passing `1`
instead of `1L` can produce unexpected behavior or an API error. This isn't
new in 3.0, but it surfaces more often now that raw integer parameters are
exposed directly instead of being hidden behind wrapper defaults.

## Worked example: before and after

```r
# ---- 2.x ----
library(synapser)
synLogin()

project <- Project("My Project")
project <- synStore(project)

file <- File(path = "data.csv", parentId = project$properties$id)
file <- synStore(file)

file <- synGet(file$properties$id, downloadFile = FALSE)
file$annotations <- c(assay = "RNA-seq")
file <- synStore(file, forceVersion = FALSE)

synDelete(project)
```

```r
# ---- 3.0 ----
library(synapser)
synLogin()

project <- Project(name = "My Project") |> synStore()

file <- File(path = "data.csv", parent_id = project$id) |> synStore()

file <- synGet(file$id, file_options = FileOptions(download_file = FALSE)) |>
  synSetProperties(annotations = list(assay = "RNA-seq"), force_version = FALSE) |>
  synStore()

synDelete(project)
```
